claims.text: Z.ai released GLM-5 on 2026-02-12 and described it as targeting complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks.
The first-party release describes 744B total parameters with 40B active, 28.5T pre-training tokens, DeepSeek Sparse Attention integration, and asynchronous RL infrastructure named slime.
The released weights are described as MIT licensed with deployment paths through frameworks including vLLM and SGLang.
Benchmark rankings and claims that GLM-5 closes the gap with frontier proprietary models are vendor claims.

limitations.text: Architecture/training figures are first-party technical disclosures, not independently audited.
The model’s release and license can be verified independently from its claimed performance.
